title: Section 107 — Abetment of suicide of child or person of unsound mind

content.overview: BNS s. 107 — Abetment of suicide of child or person of unsound mind.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Abetment of suicide of a child or a person of unsound mind (old IPC 305). This is the aggravated sibling of s. 108. The person who dies must be a child (below 18 — s. 2) or of unsound mind. The accused is the abettor, not the deceased. Read abetment with ss. 45–46: instigation, conspiracy or aid.
In student language: BNS s. 107 is the rule on “Abetment of suicide of child or person of unsound mind”. The section provides that if any child, any person of unsound mind, any delirious person or any person in a state of intoxication, commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 107 exists so that “Abetment of suicide of child or person of unsound mind” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

learningObjectives: Master the aggravated offence of abetting the suicide of a child or person of unsound mind under BNS s. 107.
Analyze the protected classes: children (under 18), persons of unsound mind, delirious persons, and intoxicated persons.
Recognize the severe sentencing framework: death, imprisonment for life, or up to ten years, and fine.
Contrast s. 107 with general abetment of suicide under s. 108.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 107 provides that if any child, any person of unsound mind, any delirious person or any person in a state of intoxication, commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Imposes capital and life sentences for abetting the suicide of vulnerable persons who lack full mental capacity, reflecting high moral and penal culpability.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 107 (corresponding to IPC s. 305).
Victim categories: Child (under 18 years), person of unsound mind, delirious person, person in a state of intoxication.
Actus reus: Abetting the commission of suicide (by instigation, conspiracy, or intentional aiding).
Result: Suicide is actually committed by the vulnerable victim.
Punishment: Death, or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: The person who committed suicide was a child (under 18), person of unsound mind, delirious person, or intoxicated person.
The accused abetted the commission of such suicide.
The abetment was the proximate cause leading to the suicide.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 107 penalizes abetment of suicide when targeted against individuals who suffer from diminished capacity or heightened vulnerability: minors under eighteen years, persons of unsound mind, delirious individuals, or persons in an intoxicated state. Because these victims lack the mature mental capacity to resist manipulation, instigation, or psychological pressure, the law treats abetting their suicide with the utmost gravity—equating it to capital homicide. The punishment ranges from death to imprisonment for life, or a term of up to ten years, and fine. Abetment must satisfy the legal standards of Section 45 BNS: active instigation, conspiracy, or intentional aid directly provoking the suicide.
examples: Teaching example (Instigating a distressed child): An adult continuously bullies, blackmails, and commands a 14-year-old school student to jump from a building, providing instructions and telling the child they have no right to live. The child commits suicide. The adult is liable under s. 107 (capital/life tier).

Teaching example (Exploiting an intoxicated person): An accused encourages a heavily intoxicated person who is disoriented to swallow a bottle of lethal pesticide, handing him the bottle. The person swallows it and dies. This constitutes abetment of an intoxicated person under s. 107.
distinctions: Section 107 vs Section 108: Section 107 applies to children and mentally incapacitated persons, carrying death or life imprisonment; Section 108 applies to sane adults, carrying up to ten years imprisonment.
Abetment of suicide (s. 107) vs Murder (s. 101): In murder, the accused causes death; in abetment of suicide, the victim performs the fatal act upon themselves under the accused's instigation.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who repeatedly urged a mentally ill person residing in an asylum to hang herself, supplying the rope, is punishable under s. 107.
Rule: Abetting the suicide of a person of unsound mind is punishable with death, life imprisonment, or up to ten years under BNS s. 107.
Application: The victim was of unsound mind, the accused provided active aid and instigation, and suicide was committed.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 107.

keyTakeaways: Applies to suicides of children under 18, persons of unsound mind, delirious, or intoxicated.
Requires proof of actual abetment (instigation, aid, or conspiracy).
Carries severe penalty: death, life imprisonment, or up to ten years, and fine.
Aggravated counterpart to general suicide abetment under s. 108.
